title: ABACUS silently sets symmetry to 0 (`Automatically set symmetry to 0 and continue`) so symmetry=1 gives almost no speedup
symptom: A graphene+H2O slab/delta-ST pilot with `symmetry = 1` in INPUT printed a warning that the optimised reciprocal/real-space lattice does not match and `Automatically set symmetry to 0 and continue`; the comparison of real vs reciprocal Bravais lattices was inconsistent. In the same family, ABACUS identified only 1 structural symmetry operation although k still dropped 16 -> 10, and `nks=10` was not divisible by `kpar=4` (load-balance warning only).
root_cause: ABACUS derives its symmetry from the real-space lattice produced by the input; a hexagonal cell written with ~1e-5 Angstrom lattice-vector rounding gives a real/reciprocal Bravais determination mismatch, so ABACUS disables symmetry for safety, and a one-leg adsorbate slab or non-ideal C coordinates genuinely break the mirror symmetry anyway. Writing `symmetry 1` in INPUT therefore does not guarantee that the symmetry lane runs.
minimal_fix: Before claiming symmetry acceleration, grep the ABACUS log for `Automatically set symmetry to 0` and for the number of symmetry operations actually found; if the message appears, fix the lattice-vector geometric rounding (1e-5 Angstrom level, without changing relative atomic positions) or accept a non-symmetry run. Choose `kpar` to divide the actual `nks` after symmetry reduction.
validation: Confirm the log shows the warning absent and reports the expected symmetry operation count, and that nks/nq equals the expected irreducible count (e.g. 10 for a 4x4x1 slab with the real structure). Compare the number of written q files with the expected irreducible set before scheduling production jobs.
avoid: Do not write `symmetry 1` and assume k/q reduction happened - inspect the log. Do not treat a `kpar` non-divisibility warning as the reason for a slow symmetry run; the real reason is usually that symmetry was auto-disabled.
